                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-erasmus-impact-study-effects-of-mobility-on-the-skills-and-employability-of-students-and-the-internationalisation-of-higher-education-institutions" target="_blank">The Erasmus Impact Study: Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions</a></div>

Hast du schon mal eine Person eingestellt und gewusst: Diese eine Entscheidung verändert die ganze Firma?

Hast du schon mal erlebt, wie eine einzige falsche Besetzung ein kleines Team um Monate zurückwirft?

Und hast du dir schon mal gewünscht, nicht die 30. Rolle des Jahres abzuarbeiten, sondern bei jeder Einstellung wirklich mitzugestalten, wohin ein Unternehmen wächst?

Bei FINE DINE ist jede Einstellung genau das: ein Hebel. Wir sind heute 11 Leute und wachsen auf 15 bis 20. Bis 2030 wollen wir die FINE DINE Box in mehr als 100 Städte in Europa bringen. Jede Person, die du zu uns holst, entscheidet mit darüber, ob uns das gelingt. Du suchst aus, wer diesen Weg mit uns geht.

Was uns wirklich ausmacht: Wir drei Founder denken seit Jahren an kaum etwas anderes als an FINE DINE. Bei uns zählt das Ergebnis, nicht wie viele Stunden jemand im Büro sitzt oder wie schön eine Präsentation aussieht. Entscheidungen fallen schnell, Wege sind kurz, und du arbeitest direkt mit uns Foundern zusammen. Du arbeitest People & Culture bei uns nicht in einem bestehenden System ab. Du baust es auf.

Bist du an Bord?

🎁🎟 Mit der FINE DINE® Box verbinden wir Top-Restaurants und Genießer.

🇩🇪🇨🇭 Bereits in 17 Städten in Deutschland und der Schweiz vertreten.

👨‍🍳😋 Wir vermitteln jährlich mehr als 250.000 Restaurantbesuche.

👔✍🏻 Erfolgreiche Finanzierungsrunde 2022 mit renommierten Investoren.

🏢🗞️ Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Deutschlands größten Medienhäusern (Süddeutsche Zeitung, F.A.Z. etc.).

Aufgaben

  • Recruiting Ownership: Du verantwortest das Recruiting für ca. 5 Rollen pro Jahr, strategisch und operativ. Von der Bedarfsklärung mit uns Foundern über Stellenanzeigen und strukturierte Interviews bis zum Angebot.
  • Active Sourcing: Du findest Key-Hires per Direktansprache über LinkedIn und dein Netzwerk, in der Region Ulm und darüber hinaus.
  • Recruiting-System: Du baust das Fundament für schnelles und nachhaltiges Recruitment auf: Pipeline, Scorecards, Interviewleitfäden und KPIs wie Time-to-Hire, Response-Rate und Conversion.
  • Sparringspartner für die Founder: Du berätst deine Hiring Manager auf Augenhöhe und mit Daten.
  • Employer Branding & Content: Du machst FINE DINE als Arbeitgeber sichtbar. Du baust unsere LinkedIn-Präsenz von null auf, postest regelmäßig über Team, Kultur und unseren Alltag, holst das Team mit ins Boot und schreibst Stellenanzeigen, die zeigen, wer wir wirklich sind.
  • Onboarding & Ansprechperson: Du bist Ansprechperson für unser Team und sorgst dafür, dass neue Kolleg:innen schnell ankommen und ab Tag 1 produktiv sind.
  • People Operations: Du stimmst dich mit unserem Steuerbüro und der Lohnbuchhaltung ab und bist die erste Ansprechperson für alle HR-Themen im Team.

Qualifikation

  • Recruiting-Erfahrung: Du bringst Erfahrung im Recruiting mit, idealerweise in-house in einem Start-up oder Scale-up in enger Zusammenarbeit mit den Foundern oder in einer Personalberatung.
  • Active Sourcing: Direktansprache ist dein Steckenpferd. Du schreibst Nachrichten, auf die Menschen antworten, und kennst deine Conversion-Raten von Outreach bis Hire.
  • Lernbereitschaft: Du willst mehr als „nur“ Recruiting und hast Lust, dir neue Themen wie Employer Branding, Payroll oder Onboarding eigenständig zu erarbeiten.
  • Eigenverantwortung & Speed: Du arbeitest schnell, hands-on und eigenverantwortlich. Du lieferst in Tagen, nicht in Wochen, und misst dich an Ergebnissen statt an Aktivitäten.
  • Datenkompetenz & Kommunikation: Du steuerst nach Zahlen, nicht nach Bauchgefühl, und hast Zielwerte wie Time-to-Hire im Kopf.
  • Stressresistenz: Du bleibst ruhig, wenn mehrere Prozesse und Projekte parallel laufen und ein Wunschkandidat kurzfristig absagt.

Ein Plus, aber kein Muss

  • LinkedIn & Content: Du hast erste Erfahrung mit LinkedIn-Content oder Employer Branding. Falls nicht, lernst du bei uns, wie man Content strategisch aufbaut.
  • Branchenerfahrung: Du kennst D2C, E-Commerce oder Premium-Consumer-Brands und hast Marketing-, Sales- oder Tech-Rollen besetzt.
  • HR-Admin: Du hattest schon Berührungspunkte mit Payroll, Arbeitsverträgen oder Onboarding-Prozessen.
  • Aufbauerfahrung: Du hast schon einmal einen Bereich von null aufgebaut.

Benefits

  • Gehalt: 60.000 € fix + 10.000 € variabel bei klarer Zielerreichung, also 70.000 € OTE.
  • Impact: Du übernimmst eine Schlüsselrolle in dem Bereich, der für unser Wachstum am wichtigsten ist.
  • Team: Du arbeitest mit einem extrem ambitionierten Team und direkt mit den drei Foundern zusammen, mit echtem Entscheidungsspielraum ab Tag 1.
  • Personal Growth: Du wächst über Recruiting hinaus in Employer Branding, People Ops und HR-Admin, mit Einarbeitung und direktem Sparring mit den Foundern.

Du willst mit uns wachsen? Dann bewirb dich jetzt!

Arbeite direkt mit unseren Gründern zusammen, treibe unser Geschäft weiter voran und komm in unser einzigartiges Team!

Wir freuen uns über deinen Lebenslauf und eine kurze Nachricht, in der du beschreibst, warum du Lust auf den Job hast.

Taktile empowers financial institutions to transform into truly AI-native organizations.   • Bring market insight back into Taktile: what insurers need, how competitors and incumbents position, and what that means for our product, messaging and pricing

  • Help build the playbook for Taktile's insurance business in DACH as we scale the team

    About Finom
    Finom is growing fast, and Finance needs data that grows with it. As our Lead Analytics Engineer for Finance, you'll be the data partner for treasury, reconciliation and accounting. You'll also support our corporate finance and investor reporting work together with the team's existing data partner. You'll build and scale the data model behind these areas, set standards, integrate the systems Finance relies on and bring in automation, including agents, where it saves real work

    This isn't a "build what's in the ticket" role. You'll learn how Finance works and why, understand where the value is, and work with the team on how their processes run, proposing improvements and the data and tools to support them. You'll report to the Head of Central Data

    What You Will Be Doing
    - Partner with the Treasury, Reconciliation and Accounting teams on their processes, priorities and how data supports them.
    - Build out treasury data: positions, cash flows and liquidity, as trusted data products the team can rely on day to day.
    - Build and scale reconciliation, so that matching, breaks and exceptions are handled systematically rather than by hand.
    - Support Accounting with the data, checks and integrations behind their close and day-to-day work.
    - Support our corporate finance data partner on corporate finance and investor reporting, working from one shared model and set of definitions.
    - Design and evolve the Finance data model, entities and metrics, with tests, lineage and documentation, so the team can reuse and extend them.
    - Set data standards and quality checks for Finance data, and build integrations with the systems Finance uses.
    - Bring automation and agents into Finance workflows where they remove recurring manual work.
    - Look at how Finance processes run today, identify what can work better and connect each piece of data work to its business cost and value.


    How We Work
    You'll have high autonomy. You choose the tools and the approach, including trialling new vendors and open-source solutions. Sign-off is needed in two cases. The first is architecture: whether a solution scales, holds across use cases and growing volumes, and runs without constant support. The second is anything that feeds high-stakes decisions. Priorities are set by final business impact.


    Who You Are
    - You've worked in or closely with Finance: in a finance team, as a finance data partner, or in data work centred on treasury, reconciliation, accounting or FP&A.
    - You understand how a finance function works: the close, cash and liquidity, reconciliations and the reports that come out of them.
    - You write expert SQL and have strong dimensional or semantic data modelling skills.
    - You've built metrics and data products that other teams depend on.
    - You have ETL and data warehouse or lakehouse experience, including onboarding sources end to end.
    - You choose precision over speed when the two conflict.
    - You work like a consultant to the business: you understand how a process works, propose solutions and frame them in terms of business value.


    Nice to Have
    - Databricks and Unity Catalog
    - Experience integrating ERP, accounting, banking or treasury systems
    - Experience with workflow automation or agents in finance processes
    - CI/CD, orchestration and infrastructure-as-code
    - Background in fintech, banking or payments


    How You'll Grow
    In your first months you get to know Finance, the model, the stack and your stakeholders. By six months you're self-sufficient and make judgement calls on scope and design without escalating. From there, you set long-term goals together with your Finance stakeholders, own the data roadmap for treasury, reconciliation and accounting, and mentor others on analytics-engineering practice.

    The Team

    The GBS Master Data Management Supplier Engagement Lead is a new role and is responsible for establishing and leading a proactive, business-facing supplier engagement and governance function within Global Business Solutions (GBS).

     

    The role will act as the primary point of coordination between suppliers, clinics, Country Finance, Procurement and GBS, ensuring that new suppliers are onboarded efficiently, accurately and in accordance with established master data governance standards, financial controls and procurement policies.

     

    Leading a team of GBS Regional Supplier Engagement SMEs, the role will drive a consistent, standardised approach to supplier onboarding, validation, engagement and ongoing supplier data quality across all operating countries.

     

    A key focus will be to embed preventative controls at the point of supplier creation, ensuring supplier records, payment methods, payment terms, banking information and supporting documentation are accurate, complete and appropriately authorised before being established in Oracle.

     

    The role will also support and be consulted on the targeted supplier data improvement and remediation initiatives, including Direct Debit and Payment Terms Rationalisation, working collaboratively with Procurement, PTP and Country Finance to reduce payment exceptions, strengthen compliance and improve end-to-end Procure-to-Pay performance.

    * Implement preventative controls to minimise duplicate suppliers, incomplete records, incorrect payment arrangements and unauthorised supplier creation
    * Ensure exceptions to supplier onboarding standards are documented, approved and escalated in line with established governance
    * Establish clear ownership and approval requirements between Clinics, Country Finance, Procurement and GBS
     

    Supplier Engagement & Stakeholder Management

     
    * Act as the primary escalation and coordination point for supplier onboarding issues

    * Coordinate resolution of complex supplier onboarding cases and ensure clear accountability for outstanding actions
    * Drive supplier and clinic education to improve the quality of submissions and reduce avoidable queries
     

    Supplier Master Data Quality & Continuous Improvement

     
    * Partner with the Customer & Supplier Master Data Lead to define supplier data quality standards and validation requirements
    * Develop supplier data quality reporting and root-cause analysis to identify recurring onboarding issues
    * Lead supplier-facing remediation activities, coordinating the collection and validation of information required to correct existing records
    * Identify opportunities to simplify and automate supplier onboarding, documentation collection and validation workflows
    * Support integration of newly acquired clinics and their supplier populations into the standard GBS supplier governance framework
     

    Supplier Engagement Operational Performance & Governance

     
    * Establish service standards, KPIs and reporting for supplier onboarding, engagement, data completeness and governance compliance
    * Monitor onboarding backlogs, supplier response times, outstanding documentation and ageing exceptions
    * Work closely with Genpact to ensure validated supplier requests are processed accurately and within agreed service levels
    * Monitor recurring BPO processing issues, escalate service failures and coordinate corrective actions with the MDM Lead
    * Maintain clear audit trails for supplier validation, approvals, exceptions and remediation activities
    * Provide regular performance updates, risks and improvement recommendations to GBS leadership
     

    Regional Team Leadership & Capability Development

     
    * Lead and develop the four Regional Supplier Engagement SMEs, ensuring consistent service delivery across supported countries
    * Define regional responsibilities, workload allocation, escalation routes and performance expectations
    * Establish standard operating procedures, training materials and consistent governance practices
    * Build regional expertise in supplier onboarding requirements, language needs and local regulatory considerations
    * Drive an ownership and continuous improvement culture across the Supplier Engagement function
    * Support the future evolution of supplier engagement capabilities, including supplier self-service and workflow automation

    * Demonstrated experience in supplier onboarding, supplier master data governance, vendor creation processes and supplier data quality management

    * Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience identifying data quality issues, conducting root-cause analysis and implementing sustainable improvements

    THE POSITION

    ANYFIELDS measures antennas by infrared thermography: a thermosensitive film heated by the radiated field is imaged by an infrared camera, giving a 2D map of the electric field, nonintrusive and very close to the antenna. Two limits remain: the maps are noisy (dynamic range of 25 to 30 dB at best, 35 to 40 dB needed to retrieve side lobes and cross-polarization), and they are blurred by the response of the detector (film and optics), whose resolution is not explained by the theory.

    This internship develops physics-driven neural networks, trained without any clean reference, to restore the maps, and compares them rigorously with the conventional methods already implemented.

    Missions :

    • Benchmark synthetic and measured datasets, reproduction of the conventional methods (wavelet denoising, drift removal, deconvolution, slanted edge).

    • Estimate PSF of the detector: neural network constrained by the film heat diffusion and the optics, estimated from a few measurements; explain the gap between the theoretical (about 1 mm) and measured (4 to 8 mm) resolution. Compare with conventional methods.

    • Implement Denoising by self-supervised deep denoising of the maps, quantified gain in dB towards 35 to 40 dB, ranking of the limiting factors of the setup.

    • Validate by test whether the imaging resolves the individual elements of array antennas in the Ku and Ka bands, before and after improvement. Report on the retained methods.

    You will work at the crossroads of electromagnetics, imaging and deep learning, with the engineers of the Innovation team.

    Location: Toulouse (city centre)

    Start: As soon as possible

    Duration: 6 months

    Profile

    • Bac+5 - Engineering school / Master in applied mathematics, signal and image processing, machine learning and/or electromagnetics

    • Programming skills (preferably Python), experience with a deep learning framework

    • Knowledge of inverse problems or infrared cameras is a plus

    • Team spirit, proactive attitude and good communication skills in an interdisciplinary team

    About EH Energy Engineering

    EH Energy is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy-duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product delivers a significantly more compact fuel cell system with high power density and lower production costs. In response to the challenges of climate change and the global shift toward decentralized energy, EH Energy provides high-performance, cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

    To support our rapid growth and bring our systems to global markets, we are seeking a Certification Engineer. In this critical role, you will take full ownership of our product compliance roadmap, bridging the gap between innovative engineering and strict global regulations. You will lead hazard and risk assessments, define certification strategies across international markets (EU, North America, marine), and interface directly with notified bodies and classification societies to ensure our fuel cell systems are safe, fully compliant, and market-ready.

    This role requires a full-time, on-site presence at our office in Nyon, Switzerland. We are unable to offer remote or hybrid arrangements, so candidates should be based locally or prepared to relocate.

     

    Key responsibilities

    Certification strategy and project management

    • Identify applicable directives, regulations, harmonised standards and class rules early in the development cycle and translate them into design requirements (EU, North America, marine)

    • Select and manage notified bodies, NRTLs, classification societies and test laboratories, own budgets, schedules and contracts for certification work

    • Plan and witness type tests, factory acceptance tests (FAT) and site acceptance tests (SAT)

    Safety engineering and risk analysis

    • Lead risk assessments to ISO 12100 and hazard studies (HAZID, HAZOP to IEC 61882)

    • Lead design and process FMEA (IEC 60812) for stacks, balance of plant, containers and fuel processing

    • Run explosion-protection assessments: hazardous area classification (IEC 60079-10-1), ventilation and gas detection concepts, and equipment selection

    • Specify and verify safety functions to ISO 13849 (PL) and IEC 61508, including safety requirement specifications and validation reports

    Compliance and technical documentation

    • Compile and maintain technical construction files, CE Declarations of Conformity, type-approval dossiers and certification reports

    • Write and review user, installation, operation and maintenance manuals, safety instructions and labelling

    • Maintain the standards register and assess the impact of new or revised standards

    • Manage certification change control: assess design changes for impact on existing certificates

    Collaboration and continuous improvement

    • Act as the internal authority on certification scope: ensure in-service conformity of series production with certified designs, and support procurement and supply chain on material and packaging compliance (e.g. RoHS, packaging regulations).

    • Support design reviews and supplier qualification, including component certificates (ATEX, PED, electrical)

    Standards and regulatory scope

    The role covers, but is not limited to, the frameworks below. Working knowledge of most is expected; deep expertise in several is required

    • IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1:2021, ISO 16110-1 and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230

       

    Required qualifications

    • Master’s or bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, chemical, process or safety engineering, or equivalent

    • 5+ years in product certification, compliance or safety engineering for complex electromechanical or process equipment (energy, gas, process, machinery or marine)

    • Direct experience with hydrogen or fuel cell systems and the IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1 or ISO 16110

    • Proven track record of taking products through CE marking and third-party certification with notified bodies or NRTLs

    • Hands-on experience leading FMEA, HAZOP and risk assessments, and documenting them to auditor standard

    • Solid knowledge of ATEX / IECEx, hazardous area classification and explosion-protection concepts

    • Experience specifying and validating safety functions to ISO 13849 and/or IEC 61508

    • Excellent technical writing: clear, structured, audit-ready technical files and manuals

    • Fluent English, written and spoken

       

    Preferred qualifications and personal profile

    Nice to have

    • Marine type approval with a classification society (DNV, LR, BV, ABS) or IGF Code projects

    • Experience with fuel processing, reformers or fire equipment, and with pressure equipment under PED

    • Certified functional safety qualification or ATEX/IECEx competence certification

    • Familiarity with North American codes (NEC, NFPA) and UL/CSA certification

    Personal profile

    • Rigorous and structured, with a strong safety mindset and an eye for detail

    • Pragmatic: finds compliant solutions that keep development moving

    • Confident communicator with engineers, auditors, authorities and customers

    • Self-driven in a fast-growing, scale-up environment; comfortable owning topics end to end

       

    Start date: Immediately

    • Hands-on experience with stack test benches, cell voltage monitoring, EIS and durability/AST protocols.

    • Management experience

    About MotherDuck

    Don’t let the quirky name fool you: At MotherDuck, we’re on a mission to make data warehousing fun, frictionless, and ducking awesome for developers and data practitioners building blazing fast internal and customer-facing analytics experiences. We're building a cloud-hosted version of DuckDB, working hand-in-hand with the creators of the fastest-growing and fastest-improving query engine on the planet. Unlike other databases, MotherDuck was architected to unify local development with cloud operations to bridge the gap between software and data engineering workflows. Our team is a mix of thoughtful, passionate, and empathetic data industry veterans.

    What you will do

    The Database team is the bridge between DuckDB and the cloud. We own the core server and client extension logic that lets DuckDB run seamlessly, whether it's local or in the cloud, and we work in C++ right alongside the DuckDB codebase itself. Our mission is to push the boundaries of embedded database performance, distributed execution, and user experience, all while staying closely connected to DuckDB Labs (the team behind DuckDB) to align on APIs and shape what's next.

    Day to day, we drive major projects in dual execution, resource assignment, and system reliability, while also handling incoming issues and lending our DuckDB expertise to other teams. We collaborate closely across MotherDuck and with the wider DuckDB community, making sure people get the best of both local and cloud worlds.     This role is ideally based in Amsterdam or Berlin, but we are also open to great candidates remotely in Europe.

    • Lead cross-functional work with our frontend, platform, and infrastructure teams to keep the user experience coherent end to end.

    • Push the state of the art in embedded database performance, distributed execution, and DuckDB internals.

    • Deepen your DuckDB expertise and share it with the rest of the company through mentorship and documentation.

    • Work directly with our support team to debug issues, learn from real usage patterns, and prioritize the improvements that matter most.

    • Improve systems holistically... spotting architectural challenges early and clearing bottlenecks before they become problems.

    • Mentor teammates and help raise the bar for engineering practices across the team.

    • Work closely with DuckDB Labs (which grew out of the Database Architectures group at CWI, where vectorized execution and DuckDB were born) to help align on APIs and shape where DuckDB goes next.

    What you bring

    • You've built and shipped complex backend systems, and you know what great looks like.

    • You're fluent in a backend language like C++, Rust, Java, or similar systems languages, and you're comfortable working close to the metal. (C++ and Rust are the biggest plus here, and we love a great Java engineer too.)

    • A good foundation in query engines, execution plans, indexing, and performance optimization techniques.

    • Hands-on experience with DuckDB is a huge plus, no matter what level you're coming in at.

    • You've worked with cloud infrastructure, networking, and building low-latency distributed systems.

    • You can scope and lead projects that span multiple collaborators and cross-functional dependencies.

    • You take pride in clear thinking, careful design, and thoughtful tradeoffs.

    • You're comfortable mentoring peers and helping build a collaborative, high-agency environment.

    • You enjoy engaging with the wider community, whether that's open-source conversations or working directly with DuckDB Labs.

The Opportunity<\/h2>

AI is fundamentally changing how enterprises operate.<\/p>

For decades, procurement teams have relied on spreadsheets, emails, and fragmented processes to manage billions of dollars in spend. As AI agents become capable of taking over increasingly complex workflows, the way companies run procurement is about to change.<\/p>

              Our Story<\/strong><\/h3>

              At Endear, we\u2019re building the first modern CRM for retail teams, starting with the frontline.<\/p>

              <\/p>

              Our software helps retail teams build stronger customer relationships through thoughtful, intuitive technology. From clienteling and customer capture to appointments and in-store experiences, Endear gives brands the tools they need to create more personal interactions and drive measurable growth.<\/p>

              <\/p>

              We work with brands like Gorjana, Reformation, and Alo Yoga, and we\u2019re continuing to evolve Endear into an increasingly AI-first product built around how modern retail teams actually work.<\/p>

              <\/p>

              Position Overview<\/strong><\/p>

              We're looking for a Product Manager to help shape and deliver the next generation of Endear's platform.<\/p>

              <\/p>

              You'll take ownership of product decisions, priorities, and outcomes, working closely with Design, Engineering, and cross-functional stakeholders to turn customer needs and business opportunities into impactful product experiences.<\/p>

              <\/p>

              This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who can operate autonomously, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and drive initiatives from discovery through launch and iteration. You'll have meaningful ownership over what gets built, why it matters, and how we measure success, while partnering with product leadership on broader vision and direction.<\/p>

              <\/p>

              • Take ownership of product initiatives from discovery through launch, making decisions around scope, priorities, and tradeoffs.<\/p><\/li>

              • Partner closely with Sales, Customer Experience, and Marketing to gather insights, align priorities, and identify opportunities for product improvement.<\/p><\/li>

                • Independently own meaningful areas of the product roadmap, driving decisions and measurable outcomes within the broader product strategy.<\/p><\/li>

                • Deliver product improvements that increase adoption, engagement, customer value, and business performance.<\/p><\/li>

                • Become a trusted cross-functional partner who brings clarity to complex problems and drives alignment around priorities and decisions.<\/p><\/li>

                • Demonstrate clear business impact through the products you build and the improvements you deliver.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

                  <\/p>

                  • You love owning product decisions and are comfortable being accountable for outcomes, not just execution.<\/p><\/li>

                  • You're able to operate independently, navigate ambiguity, and make sound decisions without needing constant direction.<\/p><\/li>

                  • You think commercially and understand how product decisions connect to customer value, adoption, retention, and business growth.<\/p><\/li>

                  • You naturally bring together different perspectives from Sales, CX, Marketing, Design, and Engineering to make better product decisions.<\/p><\/li>

                        <\/p>

                        At Endear, we live by five core principles. Here's how they translate into what we're looking for in this role:<\/p>

                        • Customer First:<\/strong> You prioritize real customer problems, use research and data to guide decisions, and connect product improvements to meaningful customer and business outcomes.<\/p><\/li>

                          <\/p>

                          Endear's product organization works across three product areas: AI, IRL (in real life), and Core Flows.<\/p>

                          <\/p>

                          You'll collaborate closely with Product, Design, and Engineering while working across the business to understand customer needs, identify opportunities, and drive product outcomes.<\/p>

                          <\/p>

                          You'll partner most closely with:<\/p>

                          • Product Leadership:<\/strong> Align on broader product vision, strategic priorities, and business goals while independently owning decisions within your product initiatives.<\/p><\/li>

                          • Design Team:<\/strong> Collaborate on discovery, problem definition, prototyping, and delivering intuitive product experiences.<\/p><\/li>

                          • Engineering Team:<\/strong> Evaluate technical feasibility, navigate tradeoffs, and turn product decisions into shipped solutions.<\/p><\/li>

                          • Sales, Customer Experience & Marketing:<\/strong> Gather customer and market insights, align on product priorities, support launches, and identify opportunities to improve adoption and customer value.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

                            We're a small team with big ambitions, collaborative, customer-obsessed, and deeply excited about the problems we're solving in retail.<\/p>

                            <\/p>

                            Our Hiring Process<\/strong><\/h3>

                            1. Recruiter Screen<\/p><\/li>

                            2. Behavioral Interview with the Hiring Manager + Co-Founder<\/p><\/li>

                            3. Panel interview with key Product and Engineering team members<\/p><\/li>

                            4. Final conversation with Co-Founder + CTO<\/p><\/li>

                            5. Offer \ud83c\udf89<\/p><\/li><\/ol>

                              <\/p>

                              Compensation & Benefits<\/strong><\/h3>

                              • Base Salary: $140,000-$170,000<\/p><\/li>

                              • Fully remote, US-based team<\/p><\/li>

Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows

  • Next.js (App Router)

  • Clerk for authentication

  • Convex for data + backend logic

  • n8n (self-hosted via Docker or n8n Cloud) for workflow automation

Public page

Authenticated experience

We're hiring a Senior Copywriter – Demand Generation & Email for our client, a fast-growing, AI-first technology company transforming how global brands manage social media engagement and customer conversations.

Our client has worked with some of the world's biggest brands, including Netflix, Uber, Sephora, Benefit Cosmetics, and JD Sports.

We're looking for a creative, commercially minded copywriter who understands B2B buyer psychology, knows how to get senior decision-makers to respond, and can use AI to create smarter, more effective campaigns.

A Day in the Role

You'll review campaign performance, develop compelling B2B outreach sequences, and experiment with messaging that gets senior decision-makers to respond.

You'll also collaborate with sales and marketing teams, refine AI personalization workflows, and turn campaign insights into stronger, better-performing copy.

Your goal? Write emails that don't just get opened but start conversations and drive results.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Write B2B outbound email and LinkedIn sequences targeting senior social, marketing, and customer experience leaders.

  • Plan email sequences from start to finish, including audience targeting, messaging, timing, and follow-ups.

  • Create sales follow-up emails, re-engagement campaigns, and messaging for lost opportunities.

  • Develop event invitations, post-event follow-ups, and inbound lead nurture emails.

  • Test subject lines, openings, and offers to improve campaign performance.

  • Track results, including replies, positive responses, and meetings booked.

  • Manage and improve AI-powered personalization workflows, including prompts and instructions.

  • Support newsletters, customer emails, product announcements, and content based on blogs and case studies.

Must-Have Requirements

  • Experience as a Copywriter, Content Writer, Email Marketer, or similar, with examples of B2B emails you've personally written.

  • Experience writing for a B2B software company, agency, or in-house marketing team.

  • Strong sales sense and an understanding of what makes buyers respond to or ignore an email.

  • Ability to write compelling messaging for senior social, marketing, and customer experience leaders at large brands.

  • Creativity and good judgment in identifying ideas worth testing.

  • Excellent written English, with a natural understanding of North American and UK audiences.

  • Regular use of AI in your writing process, with a clear understanding of its strengths and limitations.

  • Ability to learn new tools quickly.

  • Strong ownership, organization, and follow-through.

Nice to Have: Experience with HubSpot.

Who This Role Is For

  • You enjoy writing B2B copy that starts conversations and generates opportunities.

  • You're creative, commercially minded, and comfortable testing new ideas.

  • You understand how to combine AI with strong writing and strategic thinking.

  • You take ownership of your work and care about the results it produces.

This Role Is NOT for You If...

  • You have no experience writing B2B emails.

  • You rely entirely on AI-generated copy without applying your own judgment.

  • You aren't interested in testing and improving campaign performance.

  • You're looking for an SDR or cold-calling position rather than a copywriting role.

Why You'll Love This Opportunity

  • Fully Remote: Flexible working arrangements with a global team.

  • Competitive Compensation: Market-competitive pay.

  • Generous Time Off: 4+ weeks of paid time off.

  • Career Growth: Opportunities to lead strategic initiatives and advance into leadership roles based on performance.

  • Global Exposure: Work with internationally recognized brands and innovative AI technology.

  • Team Connections: Opportunities for global team meetups.

Think You Can Write Emails That Actually Get Replies?

We're looking for someone who understands what makes great B2B copy work and knows how to turn that knowledge into real results.

If that's you, we'd love to see what you've got!

Apply now!

The Portfolio Manager interacts with IT leadership to identify potential projects that best align to the strategic priorities of the organization, balances capacity against demand, and connects plans and resources to project execution.


The IT Portfolio Manager assesses, documents, and budgets potential projects; perform project resource planning; conducts continuous monitoring and reports on portfolio health, and participates in the department’s change management process and staff training.

  • Works to develop and implement best practices, processes, and toolsets for effective portfolio/project management, and helps educate staff on best practices and effective project execution.
  • Manages and leverages the life cycle of a wide range of cross departmental initiatives, investments, programs, projects, and outcomes to optimally achieve enterprise goals and objectives.
  • Recalibrates the portfolio as necessary when the demands of the business dictate a change in delivery or scope of work.
  • Collaborates with Project Intake Team to manage the processes of reviewing new requests, assessing project priority, and making go / no-go recommendations to Executive Steering Committee.
  • Coordinates with Enterprise PMO on management of large, strategic initiatives.

  • Provides oversight to program and project managers within the portfolio and quality assurance ensuring that initiatives are being well managed and adhering to appropriate standards and good practice; develops and facilitates regular portfolio performance review presentations for Executive Steering Committee.
  • Manages all aspects of change control and risk oversight.
  • Develops an overall understanding of each initiative in the portfolio to understand the potential customer impact and service requirements generated by each initiative in the portfolio.
  • Adheres to University and unit-level policies and procedures and safeguards University assets.

This list of duties and responsibilities is not intended to be all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other duties or responsibilities as necessary.

    Rithum™ is the world’s most trusted commerce network, accelerating how brands, suppliers, and retailers work together to deliver seamless e-commerce experiences. We provide an unmatched platform for brands and retailers, enabling them to accelerate growth, optimize operations across channels, scale product offerings and enhance margins.

    Today, more than 40,000 companies trust Rithum to grow their business across hundreds of channels, representing over $50 billion in annual GMV. Using our commerce, marketing, and delivery solutions, our customers create optimized consumer shopping journeys from beginning to end.

    Overview

    Rithum expects employees across all roles to leverage AI and technology to improve efficiency, streamline workflows, and create scalable ways of working.

    Rithum is embedding AI into every corner of how it operates — and security is no exception.

    As a Staff Information Security Engineer, you own the intersection of AI adoption and information security: designing guardrails for AI-powered products, building automated security tooling, designing security controls and monitoring for an AI-First workforce, helping every team at Rithum move fast without creating risk they cannot see. This is not a typical security role. You spend as much time building and automating as you do reviewing, turning a repeating control into infrastructure-as-code, a manual review into a workflow, and a vague AI risk into a concrete, enforced guardrails. You work autonomously, balancing research with fast-paced delivery, and collaborating closely with Platform Engineering, IT, Security Champions, and external auditors.

    Responsibilities

    • Act as the bridge between architectural intent and operational reality; mediate conflicts between security requirements and feasible implementation, propose compensating controls where gaps exist and help register, track and remediate residual risks.
    • Implement preventive, default-on security controls across cloud and enterprise environments, codified as policy- and infrastructure-as-code so security is enforced by design, including controls that govern how AI tools and models may be used.
    • Implement and enforce identity and access controls to an agreed standard, including access boundaries for AI systems and non-human/agent identities by partnering with Platform Engineering and IT to align tooling and policy to the architecture.
    • Assist in maintaining the InfoSec risk register; track emerging threats and translate them into actionable guidance for engineering teams.
    • Support third-party and vendor risk assessments, with a focus on vendors who process data through AI pipelines.
    • Automate repetitive security workflows (evidence collection, access reviews, alert enrichment) and build or operate AI-assisted security agents — with human-in-the-loop approval gates, least-privilege credentials, and explicit attention to each agent's own blast radius.
    • Integrate security tooling (SIEM, CSPM, DAST/SAST, vulnerability scanners) with LLM layers to surface actionable insight and automated responses.
    • Define and enforce security requirements for AI-powered features: model access controls, prompt-injection mitigations, output validation, and data-handling boundaries.
    • Conduct threat modelling on agentic and LLM-based systems, accounting for novel attack surfaces such as tool misuse, indirect prompt injection, and supply chain risk.

    Qualifications

    Minimum Qualifications

    • 5+ years of security engineering experience with demonstrated AI/ML security depth (prompt injection, model supply chain, adversarial inputs, RAG).
    • Experience using AI tools (ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, etc.) and LLM frameworks and APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, or similar) to accelerate and elevate your work.
    • Hands-on identity and access expertise across modern enterprise and cloud identity stacks, including access models for AI systems and non-human identities.
    • Infrastructure and policy-as-code (e.g. Terraform, OPA/Rego) and proficiency in a scripting language for automation (Python preferred).
    • Cloud security expertise: AWS Solutions Architect / Security Specialty or equivalent demonstrated expertise, including multi-account governance, preventive guardrails, and policy-as-code.
    • Application security (OWASP Top 10 and the OWASP LLM/GenAI Top 10, secure SDLC) and threat-modelling methodologies (STRIDE, PASTA, or equivalent). Practical experience building or operating AI agents, and integrating security tooling (SIEM, CSPM, SAST/DAST/SCA) so it surfaces action rather than raw alerts.
    • Working knowledge of SOC 2 and/or ISO 27001 control frameworks.

    Preferred Qualifications

    • Experience building or operating AI agents in a production environment.
    • Awareness of privacy regulation (GDPR/CCPA) as it touches AI including privacy-by-design and DPIAs.
    • Red teaming or adversarial ML research backgrounds.
    • Experience implementing privileged-access, key-management, posture-management, or data-protection programs.
    • Experience with EDR, CASB, DLP, Security automation and SAST, DAST, IAST and SCA tools.
    • Cloud Architecture or Security certifications (CCSK, TAISE, AWS).

    Travel Required

    Up to 10%

    Other Duties

    What it’s like to work at Rithum

    When you join Rithum, you can expect to work with smart risk-takers, courageous collaborators, and curious minds.

    As part of the Rithum team, you are valued, supported, and included. Guided by a transparent culture and accessible, approachable leadership, we offer career opportunities aligned to your ambitions and talents. To ensure work and life balance works for you, we also offer an array of resources to support you and your families, including comprehensive benefits and wellness plans.

    At Rithum you will:

    • Partner with the leading brands and retailers.
    • Connect with passionate professionals who will help support your goals.
    • Participate in an inclusive, welcoming work atmosphere.
    • Achieve work-life balance through remote-first working conditions, generous time off, and wellness days.
    • Receive industry-competitive compensation and total rewards benefits.

    We believe in transparency and fairness in our compensation practices.

    For this position, the expected base pay range is: $170,000-$220,000 per year.

    This range represents the base pay for the role across all U.S. locations and is determined based on market data, internal equity, and experience. Final compensation may vary depending on geographic location, skills, and relevant experience.In addition to base pay, we offer a discretionary bonus for non-sales roles, a comprehensive benefits package, and, where applicable, sales incentives.

    For this position, the expected discretionary bonus is 12% of the annual base salary.

    Benefits

    • Medical, dental and vision benefits: Affordable health care plans and company HSA contributions, starting on Day 1
    • A 6% 401(k) match
    • Competitive time off package with 20 days of Paid Time Off, 9 Company-Paid holidays, 2 paid floating holidays, 7 paid sick days, 2 Wellness days, and 1 Paid Volunteer Day; at 3 years of service PTO increases to 22 days, and at 5 years it increases to 25 days
    • 12 weeks primary caregiver leave & 4 weeks secondary caregiver leave
    • Accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity insurance
    • Pet insurance
    • Legal assistance and identity theft insurance plans
    • Life insurance 2x salary
    • Access to the Calm app and the Employee Assistance Program
    • $65/month Remote work stipend for internet
    • Culture and team-building activities

    • Charitable contribution match up to $250 per year

    • Make a meaningful impact on healthcare and disability-related decision-making nationwide

    Description

    TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We've been doing it for over five years, teaching complete beginners — people with no prior tech background — through cohort-based programs built on our own platform and curriculum, developed in partnership with Nebius AI. Our team is fully remote and globally distributed, and we serve a large, active student base across both regions.

    We are looking for a Student Retention Specialist to support students in their learning journey and help them stay committed to their educational goals.

    This role is responsible for driving student engagement, retention, and overall satisfaction by building meaningful relationships, identifying potential challenges, and providing proactive support. You will work closely with students to help them stay motivated, overcome obstacles, and successfully achieve their educational goals.

    What you will do

    • Engage with students through retention-focused calls and chats, addressing refund and cancellation requests with empathy and professionalism.
    • Identify the underlying reasons behind student dissatisfaction and provide personalized solutions to improve their experience and commitment.
    • Manage renewal and recurring payment conversations, proactively reaching out to students before their current term ends to support extensions and continued enrollment.
    • Consistently meet or exceed weekly retention (save rate) and renewal performance goals.
    • Maintain accurate and detailed records of all student interactions within CRM systems.
    • Participate in call reviews, coaching sessions, and continuous development initiatives to enhance performance and student outcomes.

    Requirements

    • 1+ years of experience in Retention, Customer Success, Sales, or another customer-facing role.
    • Fluent English communication skills, both written and verbal, as you'll be supporting English-speaking students.
    • Strong empathy, active listening, and relationship-building skills, with a genuine desire to help others succeed.
    • Comfortable working in a target-driven environment and meeting performance goals.
    • Resilient, adaptable, and able to remain calm and solution-oriented during challenging conversations.
    • Experience using CRM platforms to manage customer interactions and maintain accurate records.

    What we can offer you

    • Clear performance expectations, fast feedback loops, and full ownership of your work and results.
    • Join a mission-driven company helping thousands of people transform their careers through education and technology.
    • A fast-paced environment built on accountability, ownership, and impact—without unnecessary bureaucracy.
    • Enjoy the flexibility of working remotely with a high level of autonomy, trust, and minimal micromanagement.
    • Collaborate with talented professionals from diverse backgrounds across tech, ed-tech, and other industries.
    • Work with platforms like Notion, Miro, Google Workspace, and other digital tools that enable seamless collaboration.
    • Your work will directly contribute to improving student retention, engagement, and long-term success.

    Compensation & Schedule

    • Compensation: 1,500 USD fix + performance-based bonus per month.
    • Schedule: Monday to Friday.
    • Working Hours: Approximately 3:00 PM – 12:00 AM CET (8:00 AM – 5:00 PM Colombia time).
    • Work Arrangement: Fully remote.

      <title>Samsara: Staff Software Engineer</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote
    <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://www.samsara.com/">https://www.samsara.com/</a>
</p>

<p><strong>About the role:</strong></p>
<p>Samsara (NYSE: IOT) sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world. The platform processes 25+ trillion data points annually from IoT sensors, cameras, and connected devices across thousands of organizations, and that dataset is compounding: it grew from 4 trillion to 25+ trillion in four years. We're still early in turning that data into the products that will define how physical operations run, and we're hiring the engineers who will build what comes next.</p>
<p>We're approaching ~$2B ARR growing 30%+ year over year, with 96% of our largest customers on two or more products. The fastest-growing divisions at Samsara are tackling the hardest, most ambiguous problems at the company: building new products from scratch, applying AI and ML to massive real-world datasets, and shipping capabilities that change how organizations maintain equipment, manage fleets, and run day-to-day operations. Most of this work is zero-to-one, at billion-dollar scale.</p>
<p>We're looking for software engineers who want to define what ships next. Leveling is broad and flexible: we're hiring from Senior through Staff+, across platform and product, and we're open to shaping scope around the right person's strengths and interests. That window won't stay open long.</p>
<p><strong>This role is remote and open to candidates residing in the US. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.</strong></p>
<p><strong>You should apply if:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>You want to impact the industries that run our world.</strong>&nbsp;The software you build will have real-world stakes: helping keep the lights on, getting food into grocery stores, keeping workers safe. What ships here isn't metrics on a dashboard. It shows up on the loading dock, the job site, and the dispatch floor.</li>
<li><strong>You want to build, not maintain.</strong>&nbsp;Samsara is in full growth mode. We're building new systems from scratch, not babysitting old ones. You'd own entire problem spaces end to end, with the autonomy to set direction from day one.</li>
<li><strong>You want to work where AI meets the physical world.</strong>&nbsp;Samsara has spent a decade building the largest proprietary dataset for physical operations. More connected assets generate more data, more data trains better models, better models drive more value, and more value wins more assets. The market and the opportunity here are what set us apart, not just the models.</li>
<li><strong>You believe customers are more than a number.</strong>&nbsp;Samsara engineers have a rare closeness to end users. You'll participate in customer interviews, collaborate with product managers and customer success, and use that context to build products that solve real problems operators face every day.</li>
<li><strong>You have the curiosity and drive to figure it out.</strong>&nbsp;We're looking for people who take pride in their work and get things done at all costs. The engineers who thrive here don't wait to be told what to build. They define it, ship it, and own the outcome. The rate-limiting step on our teams isn't tooling or process. It's ambition.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>In this role, you will:</strong>&nbsp;</p>
<ul>
<li>Take ownership of technically complex, mission-critical areas and run with them. We want to point you in a direction and show up to the demo meeting impressed, not spend our weeks managing the details.</li>
<li>Define and drive technical strategy for new products and platform capabilities, from backend services and APIs to the customer-facing UI.</li>
<li>Design and ship full-stack features end to end. You'll work across backend, frontend, and potentially mobile to deliver AI-powered products that solve real operational problems.</li>
<li>Partner with product, design, and customer-facing teams to translate ambiguous, real-world problems into clear technical plans and measurable outcomes.</li>
<li>Build and scale the systems behind AI-driven products, including data ingestion, APIs, and the workflows that put intelligence into the hands of operators.</li>
<li>Raise the bar for the engineers around you through code reviews, design reviews, technical mentorship, and by setting a standard for quality, velocity, and craft.</li>
<li>Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Minimum requirements for the role:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.</li>
<li>8+ years of experience in software design and development, including building and operating production systems at scale.</li>
<li>Strong full-stack fundamentals. You're comfortable working across backend services, APIs, and frontend (web or mobile) to ship complete products.</li>
<li>Proficiency in modern languages and frameworks (Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, React, or similar).</li>
<li>Demonstrated experience leading cross-team or cross-org projects from inception through rollout, including managing ambiguity, driving alignment, and delivering measurable impact.</li>
<li>Experience building AI-powered or data-driven products. You don't need to train models, but you know how to take AI capabilities and turn them into products customers love.</li>
<li>Strong communication skills and the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.</li>
<li>A track record of building: zero-to-one products, systems you left in a meaningfully better place, or hard problems you refused to let stay unsolved.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>An ideal candidate also has:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Experience shipping AI-powered features in production, whether that's LLM-based products, agentic workflows, recommendation systems, or other customer-facing AI.</li>
<li>Comfort with modern AI-augmented development workflows (Cursor, LLMs, etc.) to multiply your output and accelerate delivery.</li>
<li>Background working with real-world operational data (telematics, sensor data, work orders, inspections) or a strong interest in learning the domain.</li>
<li>A proven track record of mentoring senior engineers and influencing engineering culture, standards, and best practices beyond a single team.</li>
<li>Side projects, open-source contributions, or other signals of curiosity and drive outside the scope of your day job.</li>
</ul>
<div class="content-pay-transparency">
<div class="pay-input">
<div class="description">
<p>The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.</p>
</div>
<div class="title">Annual Base Salary</div>
<div class="pay-range">$162,400<span class="divider">—</span>$290,000 USD</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="content-conclusion">
<p><strong>Total Rewards</strong></p>
<p>At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why&nbsp;<a href="https://www.samsara.com/company/careers/benefits">our rewards</a>&nbsp;are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.</p>
<p>Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.</p>
<p><strong>Flexible Working&nbsp;</strong></p>
<p>At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.</p>
<p><strong>Belonging at Samsara</strong></p>
<p>At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.</p>
</div>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/samsara-staff-software-engineer">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/samsara-staff-software-engineer</a></p>
</description>
