      <title>Abnormal: Director of Security Engineering</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote - USA
</p>

<h2>About the Role</h2>
<p>Abnormal AI protects organizations from the most sophisticated email and collaboration attacks using behavioral AI. Security is not a bolt-on at Abnormal; it is core to the product we sell and the trust our customers place in us. Our security organization operates a commercial cloud environment and a separate FedRAMP-authorized environment, and we are pursuing increasingly rigorous federal authorizations as we grow.</p>
<p>We are hiring a Director of Security reporting to the CISO and leading the Security Engineering organization. You will build and scale high-performing security teams, own major security programs end to end, and operate autonomously in the CISO's absence, including representing security to executive leadership, customers, and auditors.</p>
<p>This is a role for a deeply technical leader with a software engineering background who has grown into people leadership. You have built security teams from the ground up, you write and review code and architecture when it matters, and you believe the best security organizations earn their influence through partnership rather than policy enforcement.</p>
<h2>Our Security Philosophy</h2>
<p>We run security the way the best engineering-led companies do:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Security reduces toil.</strong> Our job is to make the rest of the company faster and safer at the same time. If a control adds friction without reducing risk, it is a defect.</li>
<li><strong>Paved paths, safe by default.</strong> We invest in guardrails, golden paths, and secure-by-default infrastructure so the easy choice is the secure choice. We prefer preventing classes of problems over chasing individual findings.</li>
<li><strong>Partnership over gatekeeping.</strong> Security succeeds only through deep collaboration with engineering, IT, and business teams. We embed with builders, we ship alongside them, and we take on their constraints as our own.</li>
<li><strong>Engineering-grade rigor.</strong> We treat security problems as engineering problems: automated, measurable, code-reviewed, and continuously improved.</li>
</ul>
<p>If the security cultures that value freedom and responsibility, context over control, and guardrails over gates resonate with you, you will feel at home here.</p>
<h2>What You Will Do</h2>
<ul>
<li>Serve as deputy to the CISO: act with full authority in the CISO's absence and represent the security organization to executives, customers, and regulators.</li>
<li>Lead, coach, and grow managers and senior engineers across Security Engineering and Security Operations.</li>
<li>Own the security engineering roadmap: cloud security architecture (AWS-first), detection and response, identity, vulnerability management, and secure-by-default platform investments.</li>
<li>Drive cross-functional programs with Engineering, IT, and Product, from AI security governance to data perimeter controls to federal compliance initiatives.</li>
<li>Set and defend engineering standards for the security organization: everything as code, automated where possible, measured against outcomes rather than activity.</li>
<li>Build hiring pipelines and raise the bar on every hire; own performance management, promotion cases, and succession planning within your teams.</li>
<li>Translate technical risk into business terms for the executive team and board, and translate business priorities into a coherent security strategy.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Must Haves</h2>
<ul>
<li>10+ years in security or software engineering, including 4+ years managing security teams, ideally including managers of managers or equivalent scope.</li>
<li>A genuine software engineering background: you have shipped production software, and you evaluate security solutions the way an engineer would.</li>
<li>A proven record of building and scaling high-performing security teams, with alumni who would work for you again.</li>
<li>Deep technical fluency in cloud-native environments: AWS organizations and multi-account governance, Kubernetes, identity and access, detection engineering, and modern SDLC security.</li>
<li>Demonstrated cross-functional leadership: you have earned the trust of engineering leaders and shipped security outcomes through their teams, not around them.</li>
<li>Strong written communication: you produce decision-ready documents and can drive alignment asynchronously.</li>
<li>Executive presence: comfortable presenting to C-level leadership, customers, and auditors without preparation from the CISO.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Strong Signals</h2>
<ul>
<li>You are currently a security engineering manager or senior manager at a fintech, high-growth startup, or forward-leaning enterprise, and you are ready for broader scope.</li>
<li>You have built paved-path or secure-by-default platforms that measurably reduced both risk and developer friction.</li>
<li>Experience with compliance-driven environments (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001) without letting compliance define the security program.</li>
<li>Experience securing AI/ML systems or governing AI adoption at scale.</li>
<li>You have operated in environments where security headcount was scarce and automation was the only way to scale.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Why This Role</h2>
<p>You will inherit strong teams, an executive staff that treats security as a first-class function, and a CISO who wants a true partner rather than a lieutenant. The scope is broad, the autonomy is real, and the ceiling on this role is defined by what you take on.</p>
<p>#LI-ML1</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p>Actual compensation will be determined based on several non-discriminatory factors including skills, experience, qualifications, and geographic location.<br>In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for bonus or incentive compensation, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.</p></div><div class="title">Base salary range:</div><div class="pay-range"><span>$214,200</span><span class="divider">—</span><span>$308,000 USD</span></div></div></div><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>A note on AI in our process:&nbsp;<br></strong>Abnormal AI uses AI-assisted tools to help our recruiting team prepare for candidate interviews. These tools analyze resume content and role requirements to suggest interview questions and areas for the interviewer to explore.They do not make hiring decisions or screen candidates automatically. Every decision about a candidacy is made by a person. Further, if your application is successful and Abnormal AI makes a conditional offer of employment, we will carry out pre-employment checks which must be successfully completed to progress to a final offer. All processes and pre-employment checks are in line with prevailing legislation and Abnormal AI's policies relevant to our security and privacy standards.</p>
<p>Abnormal AI is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. For our EEO policy statement please <a href="https://assets.contentstack.io/v3/assets/blt3a076cfd9753fa1f/blt9cbda641db7c0045/6a1e3d3a66aea075cd33e462/AAP_and_EEO_Statement.pdf"><span><em>click here</em></span></a>.       <title>Dremio: Software Engineer - Query Execution</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Portugal - Remote
</p>

<div class="content-intro"><h2><strong>Be Part of Building the Future</strong></h2>
<p>Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&amp;P Global. Customers rely on Dremio for cloud, hybrid, and on-prem lakehouses to power their data mesh, data warehouse migration, data virtualization, and unified data access use cases. Based on open source technologies, including Apache Iceberg and Apache Arrow, Dremio provides an open lakehouse architecture enabling the fastest time to insight and platform flexibility at a fraction of the cost.&nbsp; Learn more at&nbsp;<a class="c-link" href="http://www.dremio.com/">www.dremio.com.</a></p></div><p><strong>About the role</strong><br>Dremio’s Query Execution team builds the runtime responsible for executing analytical queries at scale. The team sits between query planning and table scans, building the systems that turn query plans into efficient, reliable execution.</p>
<p>As a Software Engineer, you’ll work with experienced engineers to build, test, and support well-scoped improvements to the execution engine. You’ll learn how Dremio’s query runtime works while contributing to areas such as query operators, expression evaluation, memory management, scheduling, and performance.<br><br><strong>What you’ll be doing</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Build and support execution-engine components: Implement, test, debug, and maintain well-defined changes to query operators, expression evaluation, execution scheduling, and resource management.</li>
<li>Develop reliable software: Write clear, maintainable Java code; add unit and integration tests; and follow established engineering practices for code review, testing, and documentation.</li>
<li>Investigate issues: Help diagnose query correctness, reliability, and performance issues using query profiles, logs, telemetry, benchmarks, and production data.</li>
<li>Learn runtime and performance fundamentals: Build familiarity with vectorized processing, concurrency, memory usage, parallelism, data exchange, and disk spilling.</li>
<li>Collaborate with the team: Work closely with senior engineers and partner teams to understand requirements, break work into manageable tasks, and deliver incremental improvements.</li>
<li>Use AI-assisted development tools: Apply AI tools to code comprehension, debugging, test generation, and documentation, while validating results through testing, review, and sound engineering judgment.</li>
<li>Grow your engineering skills: Participate actively in design discussions and code reviews, seek feedback, and steadily take on broader technical responsibility.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>What we’re looking for</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Software engineering foundation: Up to two years of professional software development experience, or equivalent experience through internships, coursework, or substantial personal projects.</li>
<li>Programming skills: Proficiency in Java or another object-oriented programming language; willingness to learn and work in a large Java codebase.</li>
<li>Computer science fundamentals: Understanding of data structures, algorithms, and basic concurrency concepts.</li>
<li>Problem-solving ability: Able to work through well-defined technical problems, ask good questions, and apply feedback to reach a solution.</li>
<li>Quality mindset: Commitment to writing tested, maintainable code and learning established development, testing, and review practices.</li>
<li>Communication and collaboration: Able to communicate progress, surface blockers early, and work effectively with teammates.</li>
<li>Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Bonus points if you have</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>
<ul>
<li>Exposure to database internals, query processing, distributed systems, or large-scale data processing.</li>
<li>Familiarity with performance-oriented software concepts such as profiling, memory management, concurrency, or vectorized processing.</li>
<li>Experience with C++, Apache Arrow, Parquet, Apache Iceberg, Spark, Hadoop, or cloud object stores.</li>
<li>Contributions to open-source projects.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul><div class="content-conclusion"><h3><strong>What we value&nbsp;</strong></h3>
<p><span>At Dremio, we hold ourselves to high standards when it comes to People, Thinking, and Action. Our Gnarlies (that's what we call our employees) communicate with clarity, drive accountability, and are respectful towards each other. We confront brutal facts and focus on results while operating with a sense of urgency and building a "flywheel". People who like to jump in and drive momentum will thrive in our #GnarlyLife.</span></p>
<p><em><span>Dremio is an equal opportunity employer supporting workforce diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other unlawful factor.</span></em></p>
<p><em><span>Dremio is committed to providing any necessary accommodations for individuals with disabilities within our application and interview process. To request accommodation due to a disability, please inform your recruiter.</span></em></p>
<p><em><span>Dremio has policies in place to protect the personal information that employees and applicants disclose to us. Please click </span></em><a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CB96QFmOX-bFy48YFOe2GO5lmdawOpKKBj8DpTgsuNg/edit?usp=sharing"><em><span>here</span></em></a><em><span> to review the privacy notice.&nbsp;</span></em></p>
<h3><strong>Important Security Notice for Candidates</strong></h3>
<p><span>At Dremio, we uphold trust and transparency as paramount values in all our interactions with customers, partners, employees, and the general public. We have been targeted by individuals creating fake domains similar to ours to scam prospects and candidates. Please note that all official communications from us will be from an @dremio.com domain. If you suspect you've been targeted by a scam, it's imperative to report the incident to your local law enforcement agencies. For more information about this type of scam, please refer to Dremio's official statement&nbsp;<a href="https://www.dremio.com/blog/stay-alert-for-fraudulent-recruitment-attempts-that-falsely-claim-association-with-dremio/">here</a>.</span></p>
<p><em>Dremio is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company that does not have a signed agreement with the Company.</em></p></div>

<p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/dremio-software-engineer-query-execution">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/dremio-software-engineer-query-execution</a></p>
</description>

Spotify Technology is our business-to-business software team, helping organizations improve how they build and deliver software. Our products, including Backstage Portal, Confidence, and Xirp, support developers and AI-powered systems as they navigate increasingly complex engineering environments.

As an Account Executive on our Commercial team, you will drive new business for Spotify Technology. You'll focus on companies with fewer than 1,000 employees, where sales cycles typically run from weeks to a few months and success depends on a repeatable, scalable sales motion. You'll manage a high volume of opportunities, work with one or a small group of decision-makers (often a hands-on engineering leader or CTO), and move deals efficiently from the first conversation to close. You'll also help shape the playbook that enables our commercial business to grow.

You'll collaborate with Sales Engineering, Marketing, Product, and Customer Success to create a seamless customer experience. Your ability to quickly understand customers' technical needs and connect them to clear business value will be key to your success.

","id":"2a55d6c9-c564-443a-be3e-a3851db5a93b","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

• Identify and pursue new business opportunities with companies of fewer than 1,000 employees. While significant inbound demand supports the pipeline, top performers will exceed targets by treating this as a “Hunter” role in addition to converting inbound demand.

• Own the full sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through demos, proposals, negotiations, and close.

• Manage a high-velocity pipeline across multiple opportunities, keeping deals moving with clear next steps and maintaining accurate pipeline and forecast data in the CRM.

• Achieve and exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets.

• Run efficient, repeatable sales processes and contribute to playbooks that help scale our commercial sales motion.

• Partner with Marketing on inbound and outbound pipeline generation, responding quickly to leads and identifying new opportunities.

• Articulate how Backstage Portal and Confidence solve developer experience challenges, including how AI is reshaping software development.

• Tell a compelling story about Spotify's internal approach to solving engineering challenges and how our products are proven internally at scale.

• Present case studies and customer success stories that demonstrate the impact and business value of our products.

• Partner with Sales Engineering on technical evaluations and ensure a smooth handoff to Customer Success to support onboarding, retention, and expansion.

• Share customer feedback with Product and internal teams to help shape the roadmap.

"},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

• You have 4+ years of experience in a quota-carrying sales role, including 2+ years in a revenue-closing role, ideally in SaaS, developer platforms, or cloud services.

• You have a proven track record of achieving and exceeding targets in a fast-paced, high-volume B2B environment, ideally selling to small and medium-sized businesses (SMB) or mid-market companies.

• You are skilled at managing fast sales cycles efficiently while maintaining a thoughtful and effective discovery process.

• You bring strong judgment when working with incomplete information, allowing you to prioritize high-potential opportunities and confidently move away from poorly qualified deals.

• You have experience selling to technical stakeholders, including CTOs, engineering leaders, developers, or DevOps teams.

• You are familiar with software development, Product Management, DevOps tools, or developer ecosystems.

• You can clearly communicate technical benefits and business value to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• You bring strong communication, presentation, negotiation, and closing skills.

• You are highly organized and disciplined in pipeline management, forecasting, and CRM hygiene.

• You are excited to help build a scalable sales motion with AI and enjoy working with innovative products in an evolving technology landscape.

"},{"text":"Where You'll Be","content":"

This role is based in New York City

We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

    Every dataset at Spotify, from the data behind creator royalties to the signals powering recommendations, is registered, published and traced through systems our team builds. We're the source of truth for what data exists at Spotify, where it lives, who owns it, and how it flows from one pipeline to the next.

    These systems sit on the critical path of the platform. Data teams use them every day to publish and find data, and other platform teams build on them for access, retention, governance and incident response. That means our work is judged on correctness and reliability, because every system built on top of ours is only as good as the metadata we provide.

    This is a backend role focused on data management, working on the problems at the core of any large data platform: running a data catalog that stays accurate at scale, capturing lineage across batch and streaming workloads, managing schemas as they evolve, and guaranteeing that consumers only read complete data. We build on open standards like OpenLineage and Apache Iceberg, and define the internal standards for naming, storage and metadata that the rest of Spotify builds against. As the platform takes on new storage technologies and new kinds of data assets, those standards and the systems behind them have to evolve with it, and you'll help decide how.

  • Keep the Platform Healthy: Take part in on-call for critical services, build in observability and quality checks by default, and use automation, including AI tooling, to reduce toil for the team and our users.

We're judged on reliability, cost efficiency and how quickly we unblock users when something breaks.     • Support engineers through regular feedback, coaching, career development, and opportunities to share knowledge.

    • Collaborate across teams to manage dependencies, solve challenges, and build shared data solutions.

    We're looking for a Global Creative Lead to shape the visual direction of Reverb and lead a talented team of graphic designers, motion designers, and producers. You'll combine creative vision with hands-on leadership, helping the team deliver distinctive, high-quality work while building an environment where people can collaborate, experiment, and grow.

    Reporting to the Director, Global Experiential & Content Production, you'll play a key role in shaping the studio's creative output and how we work together.

    ","id":"25fac63d-d4ba-48b9-80b1-b8e87b55e448","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead and develop a team of approximately 5–6 graphic designers, motion designers, and producers, supporting their creative growth and career development.

    • Shape the visual and motion design direction across Reverb projects, creating distinctive work that brings Spotify's brand and stories to life.

    • Partner with teams across brand, communications, marketing, and production to turn creative briefs into engaging visual experiences across channels and formats.

    • Guide creative development from concept through delivery, providing clear direction, constructive feedback, and thoughtful design decisions.

    • Manage project intake, priorities, budgets, timelines, and resources to help the team deliver meaningful work across multiple projects.

    • Collaborate with Reverb's creative and production leads to build a connected, effective studio and a consistent creative experience.

    • Present creative concepts and recommendations to senior stakeholders, explaining the thinking behind decisions and building alignment.

    • Work with internal teams and external creative partners to maintain design quality, manage production needs, and navigate relevant legal and licensing requirements.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You bring 8+ years of experience in graphic design, visual design, or a related creative discipline, with a portfolio demonstrating strong visual storytelling, brand identity, and motion design.

    • You have 4+ years of experience leading creative teams, with a thoughtful approach to coaching, feedback, and helping others develop their craft.

    • You're comfortable shaping creative direction across digital, social, advertising, editorial, and long-form brand content, adapting your approach to different audiences and formats.

    • You have experience using Adobe Creative Cloud, Figma, and relevant visual or motion design tools, and you're curious about how emerging technologies can support the creative process.

    • You know how to balance creative ambition with practical delivery, making thoughtful decisions around timelines, budgets, and resources.

    • You communicate creative ideas clearly and enjoy collaborating with designers, producers, and partners across different disciplines and regions.

    • You have experience working with external creative studios, production companies, and partners, including managing budgets, contracts, and production workflows.

    • You care about creating an inclusive, supportive team environment where different perspectives are valued, feedback is welcomed, and people can do their best work.

    Spotify's Legal team is growing. We're facing innovative challenges that mirror the groundbreaking industry and product at the heart of our company. As we've expanded into more than 180 markets and our business has grown tremendously, we find ourselves facing new and interesting legal issues every day — including an increasing volume of patent disputes alongside the copyright and content matters that have always been central to our work.

    As Legal Counsel, Litigation, you will work on a variety of litigation, copyright, patent, and other contentious and advisory matters, and help craft the way our company thinks about and handles them. The work we face is constantly developing, and the workload is growing faster than we can, so we will look to you to think thoughtfully about processes and policies that will help meet our goals. Your experience making risk-based assessments and proactively finding solutions to complex problems will be crucial. Significant e-discovery experience and experience conducting confidential inquiries are a plus.

    ","id":"8d54dd6d-d7e0-4298-b051-423bcec4089e","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Coordinate litigation, pre-litigation, regulatory, and other dispute matters across multiple practice areas, including copyright and patent litigation.
  • Work with outside counsel to develop case strategy, manage budgets, and drive efficient resolution of contentious disputes.
  • Partner with the business on litigation and legal risk issues and work with colleagues to fashion solutions that balance legal risk with company objectives.
  • Develop litigation case strategies, work closely with Spotify's communications team, and formulate plans to resolve disputes efficiently.
  • Plan strategically and coordinate internally with legal and non-legal personnel on issues of the moment.
  • Provide proactive advice to internal team members on dispute avoidance and resolution, including risk mitigation.
  • Identify and mitigate threats against the company, whether from partners, users, content owners, or others.
  • Handle requests for information from the company, including subpoenas and requests from law enforcement.
  • Build scalable processes to address a growing number of claims across copyright, patent, and other areas.
  • Train teams and draft workflows and policies to help establish effective internal risk mitigation procedures.
  • Stay current on developments in patent and copyright law, particularly as they affect the technology and media industries.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"
  • You hold a law degree (or equivalent) from a top-flight law school and are qualified to practice law as in-house counsel in the State of New York.
  • You have 5+ years of litigation experience at a law firm, in-house, or both, including meaningful experience with copyright litigation.
  • You have experience with e-discovery and managing complex, multi-jurisdictional disputes.
  • You have experience contributing to teams that drive successful outcomes on complex matters.
  • You have a demonstrated ability to evaluate copyright claims, work with technical experts, and develop defense strategies.
  • You have a passion for solving legal problems and can explain legal concepts — including technical copyright issues — to non-lawyers.
  • You are comfortable working with large data sets and technical subject matter; you may not be an engineer, but you can speak the language and understand the concepts.
  • You are a problem solver who can stay calm when problems come your way.
  • You have excellent judgment — you can think a problem through when you need to, but have also developed instincts that you can trust.
  • You are self-motivated and can identify and complete work that needs to be done without being instructed.
  • You can advocate for a position while balancing risk and multiple colleagues' and business considerations.
  • You can balance many simultaneous tasks and triage to make sure the right matters get your attention.
  • You're willing to roll up your sleeves and dig in on projects.
  • You work well as part of a team — both with other lawyers and with non-legal business partners.
  • You have very effective written and oral communication skills.
  • Knowledge of music, media, tech, IP, and/or consumer issues is a plus.
  • A technical background or experience with software, streaming, or audio technology patents is a plus but not required.

    At Spotify, our Subscriptions Mission focuses on creating experiences that help listeners discover the value of Spotify, become subscribers, and stay with us for the long term. By combining technology, experimentation, and a deep understanding of our users, we help connect artists and fans while building a sustainable subscription business.

    Within the Subscriptions Mission, the Subs Foundational Models Product Area is part of the Subs User Understanding Studio. We build scalable machine learning solutions that personalize the subscriber journey, from conversion through to long-term retention. Working closely with teams across the mission, we develop ML solutions that improve key business metrics, including subscriber growth, monthly active users, and Premium retention.

    We're looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join our Radius squad. You'll take ownership of impactful ML initiatives, develop and improve production models, and contribute to the foundational ML capabilities that power personalization and optimization across Subscriptions.

    Your work could include reducing friction for Free users while balancing retention and conversion, improving payment experiences to reduce Premium churn, or developing reusable models such as subscriber embeddings that support multiple products and use cases.

    ","id":"19c12e29-b6d4-4d97-9053-48238fb7c381","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead multi-week ML initiatives end to end, from translating business requirements into technical specifications to shipping models and measuring their impact on subscriber metrics
  • Own components of our ML systems, making independent technical trade-offs and keeping them observable, reliable, and well documented
  • Collaborate with a multi-functional agile team spanning user research, design, data science, product management, and engineering to build new product features that advance our mission to connect artists and fans in personalised and relevant ways

    ","id":"0eebb462-b5a2-4e3a-b830-d8ef7505b014","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
    Conduct groundbreaking research in generative audio using diffusion or flow matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas:
     
    Vocal Synthesis — Research in vocal and speech synthesis, along with related areas such as ML-based audio processing and signal processing.
     
    Post-Training — Research in post-training techniques for music generation, including preference alignment methods (such as DPO, RLHF, or KTO), reward model design and training, and reinforcement learning to improve output quality, controllability, and human preference adherence.
     
    Editing — Research in iterative music generation and audio editing, including capabilities such as stem replacement, instrumentation change, mood changes (while preserving content), tempo changes, and structure changes.
     
    You will also:
  • Run large-scale experiments with access to Spotify's extensive infrastructure and an audience of more than 700 million monthly active users.
  • Create practical applications that harness generative technologies and push the boundaries of what's possible in listening experiences.
  • Collaborate as part of a cross-functional team—working closely with scientists, engineers, product managers, designers, user researchers, and analysts—to craft innovative solutions to complex challenges.
  • Have a direct impact on Spotify's products, tools, and services, working on projects that influence the entire organization.
  • Engage with the broader research community by publishing your findings, delivering talks, and attending top conferences.

  • You have a Ph.D. in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field. Previous industry experience is helpful.

  • You have deep expertise in at least one of the focus areas above—whether that's vocal/speech synthesis, post-training alignment techniques (e.g., PPO, GRPO, DPO), or audio-to-audio generation and text-guided music editing.
  • You have publications at leading conferences such as ICASSP, ISMIR, INTERSPEECH, ICLR, AAAI, IJCAI, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, ECCV, ICCV, or related venues.

    Conduct groundbreaking research in generative audio using diffusion or flow matching models, with a focus on one or more of the following areas:
     
    Vocal Synthesis — Research in vocal and speech synthesis, along with related areas such as ML-based audio processing and signal processing.
     
    Post-Training — Research in post-training techniques for music generation, including preference alignment methods (such as DPO, RLHF, or KTO), reward model design and training, and reinforcement learning to improve output quality, controllability, and human preference adherence.
     
    Editing — Research in iterative music generation and audio editing, including capabilities such as stem replacement, instrumentation change, mood changes (while preserving content), tempo changes, and structure changes.
     
    You will also:

    The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

     

    Security engineers at Spotify protect our platform, employees, creators, and more than 700 million users. We are looking for an experienced Security Engineer to join the Detection and Response organization and help identify, investigate, and respond to threats across Spotify's environment.

     

    You will work within our detection engineering squad where the team owns alert triage, security investigations, threat hunting, and the detection engineering lifecycle. You will turn threat intelligence, incident learnings, and analyst feedback into effective detections and investigation workflows. You will partner closely with the detection infrastructure squad, which builds and operates Detection and Response platforms and telemetry pipelines, and with teams across Spotify to make sure your squad has the signals and capabilities needed to detect and respond to threats at Spotify's scale.

     

    We are a distributed team that values curiosity, sound judgment, clear communication, and continuous learning. We teach and learn from one another, adapt as the threat landscape changes, and focus our effort according to business needs and risk.

    ","id":"cb29d857-395b-401d-9749-367e666ff870","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Identify detection opportunities, define clear telemetry requirements, and partner with the detection infrastructure squad and data owners to make the signals needed for detection and investigation available.

    • Develop, test, tune, and maintain detections across endpoint, identity, cloud, SaaS, email, and other security-relevant environments.

    • Investigate and prioritize alerts, determine their security impact, and participate in incident containment and remediation.

    • Build repeatable investigation workflows and playbooks for alert triage, evidence collection, decision-making, escalation, containment, and response.

    • Improve proactive threat-identification and threat-hunting capabilities using internal telemetry and external threat intelligence.

    • Create cutting-edge AI workflows for Detection and Response that enrich alerts, gather and analyze evidence, guide investigations, and automate repetitive response work while preserving appropriate human judgment and oversight.

    • Measure detection effectiveness, identify coverage gaps, and tune detections to balance security value, fidelity, and analyst workload.

    • Use SIEM, EDR, SOAR, and related security platforms to research threats, develop detections, investigate alerts, and validate security outcomes.

    • Share knowledge, document decisions, and communicate security findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You are curious, collaborative, and comfortable making progress in an ambiguous and rapidly changing environment.

    • You have 3+ years of hands-on experience in security operations, incident response, threat detection, detection engineering, or closely related work.

    • You understand how analysts triage and investigate alerts and how detection quality affects their decisions and workload.

    • You know how to create and tune detections based on attacker behavior, available telemetry, and an expected investigation path.

    • You are experienced with security platforms such as SIEM, EDR, SOAR, or comparable monitoring and response technologies.

    • You can write code or use an automation platform to analyze security telemetry, enrich alerts, build investigation workflows, and remove repetitive work. Experience with Python or a similar language is valuable.

    • You understand modern detection-as-code practices, including GitHub, peer review, CI/CD, testing, and safely managing production detection content.

    • You have experience working with at least one major cloud platform, such as Google Cloud, AWS, or Azure.

    • You understand common threats affecting SaaS-oriented corporate and production environments.

    • You care about clear documentation, inclusive collaboration, and explaining security concepts to people with different backgrounds and levels of expertise.

    • You are excited to create and critically evaluate cutting-edge AI workflows for detection development, alert triage, security investigations, and response, while applying sound security judgment and appropriate human oversight.

    The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

    Security engineers at Spotify help protect our environment and more than 700 million users. Within Platform, our Product Security team evaluates and communicates Spotify's security posture, helping developers and leadership make informed decisions about security risks. We own the vulnerability management platform, supporting the full lifecycle of identifying, attributing, remediating, and reporting security vulnerabilities.

    As AI changes how vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited, we're evolving how Spotify responds. We're looking for a Security Engineer to help transform vulnerability findings into reliable, actionable code improvements using agentic AI. You'll build the tools, workflows, and evaluation frameworks that make automated remediation more effective, scalable, and safe, while helping developers focus on building great experiences for our users.

     

    ","id":"1ee5dcb7-a5fe-465b-91da-d42ebab374c8","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

    • Build and improve agentic AI workflows that turn security vulnerability findings into tested, review-ready code changes for engineering teams across Spotify.

    • Design and implement evaluation frameworks to measure the quality of automated fixes, including correctness, completeness, safety, build and test success, and pull request merge rates.

    • Develop tools and processes to compare remediation approaches, evaluate AI models, and continuously improve the reliability and effectiveness of generated fixes.

    • Research and apply emerging practices in AI-assisted vulnerability remediation, including prompt engineering, context engineering, and vulnerability-specific fix guidance.

    • Identify which vulnerability types are suitable for automated remediation, balancing security impact, technical feasibility, and developer experience.

    • Collaborate with developers and security stakeholders to collect feedback through code reviews, pull requests, support channels, and interactive sessions, using these insights to improve remediation quality.

    • Help shape how Spotify approaches security posture management by building scalable solutions that reduce security risks and make it easier for teams to address vulnerabilities.

    "},{"text":"Who You Are","content":"

    • You have experience in software engineering, particularly within security engineering, developer experience, or internal infrastructure.

    • You can confidently read, understand, and write code in one or more languages such as Java, Python, Scala, C++, or TypeScript.

    • You have experience designing and building scalable systems, with an understanding of software architecture and reliable engineering practices.

    • You have worked with agentic AI systems or AI-assisted development workflows and understand how to apply them to real-world engineering challenges.

    • You understand common security risks, attack vectors, and vulnerabilities, including those affecting AI and machine learning systems, and approaches to mitigating them.

    • You have experience integrating security tools or automated workflows into production engineering environments.

    • You are familiar with agentic AI frameworks and approaches to evaluating the quality, reliability, and safety of AI-generated outputs.

    • You enjoy collaborating across teams, learning from feedback, and navigating ambiguity. You're comfortable experimenting with new approaches while balancing innovation with thoughtful security decisions.

    The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

We craft voice models that match human-level emotional expressiveness, so we can deeply engage our listeners and support creators at scale. Our groundbreaking work on speech synthesis relies on state-of-the-art deep learning methods and evaluation techniques, highly efficient data processing and model serving, and capturing audio of outstanding quality from our voice talent pool.

    We're looking for a senior applied research scientist with experience in developing novel ML techniques and architectures and with a strong interest in working across a full production pipeline to produce state-of-the-art generative conversational speech-to-speech models. You'll collaborate with our engineering teams to help develop our production pipelines, explore new ideas and methods to improve quality, understanding and realism, as well as push the frontiers of what is possible with our speech technology.

    We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration.     The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work, creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

    Our team builds Groove, a platform that helps thousands of employees plan, coordinate, and deliver work across Spotify. From initiative tracking to dependency management and collaborative planning, Groove helps teams stay aligned and execute with confidence.

    We're a small, cross-functional engineering team focused on building thoughtful tools that reduce friction and help people do their best work. We move quickly, learn from user feedback, and continuously improve the experiences we build.

    ","id":"1692fccc-29f4-4525-a683-b004c2ec62b9","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do:","content":"
  • Build and evolve Groove, a fullstack platform that supports planning, collaboration, and execution across Spotify.
  • Design and deliver features including initiative tracking, planning workflows, and dependency management.
  • Work across the stack using React, TypeScript, Java, GraphQL, PostgreSQL, and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) to build end-to-end solutions.
  • Partner closely with product managers and designers to understand user needs and create intuitive, effective experiences.
  • Ensure reliability through testing, monitoring, and continuous improvement in production.
  • Participate in an on-call rotation and help respond to production incidents when needed.
  • Improve the performance, scalability, and maintainability of frontend and backend systems.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools to improve productivity while maintaining ownership of quality, correctness, and outcomes.
  • Lead the design and delivery of complex, high-impact features across the stack.
  • Own problems end-to-end, from shaping ambiguous requirements through to production-ready solutions.

    You will contribute your expertise to various music-related projects within the company, including playlist curation, creative editorial work, and cross-functional collaboration with different teams in the region and beyond. You will provide deep cultural and musical insights to create highly engaging and cohesive music experiences for listeners, extending beyond playlists, while ensuring an unbiased editorial voice for a wide array of moods, moments, and genres. Additionally, you will drive artist discovery through an extensive editorial ecosystem of playlists and tools, critically assessing music trends and user behavior to identify opportunities and emerging trends.

    You will demonstrate a team player spirit, a passion for performance-oriented analytics, and a solid understanding of Spotify’s role in the music industry both locally and globally. Additionally, you will have an editorial personality that thrives in engaging audiences through creative formats, bringing the playlists to life in innovative ways.

    You will be encouraged to make data-informed decisions while also contributing creative and cultural expertise. Above all, your work will impact the way the world experiences music and strengthen Spotify’s role as a trusted, culturally relevant voice in the music landscape!

Join us and you’ll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

    We are the Voice Production Team, the creative team behind Spotify’s AI voice experiences. We think about AI voices from a casting perspective — including voice type, age and gender — and from a performance perspective, recognizing that a voice may need to perform differently for DJ than it does for an audiobook recap. We bring expertise in voice casting, direction, recording and production, and work closely with Speak to set the quality bar for AI voice models across experiences including AI DJ, Generative AI Ads, Personalized Podcasts, Agent Voice Chat and more.

    As a Senior Product Quality Analyst, you’ll bring a dedicated evaluation perspective to the team. You’ll own how we define and measure AI voice quality, bringing together Voice Production’s creative bar, Speak’s technical bar and the wider industry bar. Your goal won’t simply be to determine whether Spotify has the “best” AI voice technology on the market. You’ll help us answer a more important question: is our technology the best at serving Spotify’s specific needs?

  • Own the quality bar for Spotify’s AI voice models, defining what “good enough” means for different products, audiences, languages and use cases.
  • Independently design evaluation rubrics and build an evaluation approach that measures qualities such as naturalness, tone, pacing, pronunciation, accent, audio quality and overall experience.
  • Plan and carry out evaluation campaigns, turning qualitative and quantitative findings into clear recommendations for Voice Production, Speak and product teams.
  • Establish an ongoing evaluation rhythm, including when and how we reassess model quality as our technology and products evolve.
  • Benchmark Spotify’s AI voices against third-party models and competitors to understand where our experiences lead, where they differ and where there are opportunities to improve.
  • Help determine appropriate quality trade-offs as Spotify expands into additional languages and regions, considering the product use case and needs of each market.
  • Partner closely with voice experts, machine learning teams, product partners and vendors to maintain a consistent quality bar across demanding and sometimes competing priorities.
  • Surface the most meaningful gaps in model performance and use evaluation insights to help influence future research and technical priorities.

    The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

    Spotify is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Authorization team within Platform. Our team builds and operates the authorization and permissioning systems that enable creators and their teams to securely access and manage their presence across Spotify. What began by supporting Spotify for Artists has grown into foundational capabilities used across Spotify, including Music, Podcasts, and Audiobooks.

    This is a backend-focused role working on systems that sit on a critical path for Spotify's creator ecosystem. You'll help us evolve these systems as they grow in scale and complexity, bringing strong backend engineering expertise while collaborating across product, frontend, and data when needed.

    • Take ownership of critical systems that enable creators, teams, agents, licensors, and other partners to securely access and manage the right content and capabilities.

    • Evolve our backend architecture to support continued growth in users, use cases, and Spotify products while maintaining high standards for reliability, performance, and security.

    • Improve the systems and workflows that enable creators to gain access to their content, profiles, and teams.

    • Make thoughtful technical decisions and trade-offs, balancing long-term architecture with solutions that meet current product and business needs.

    • Partner with engineers and cross-functional collaborators across Spotify to understand authorization needs and build reusable platform capabilities.

    • Contribute to frontend experiences and data-related work when useful, while bringing deep expertise and leadership to backend engineering.

    • Raise engineering quality through strong technical judgment, design discussions, operational excellence, and knowledge sharing across the team.

    The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

    Surfaces Moments is a ML team within the Personalization Mission focused on creating moment-based experiences across Spotify surfaces. The team owns and evolves the experiences that help listeners quickly connect with the content that matters most to them, including the Home Shortcuts experience and the underlying intelligence that powers it. By combining cutting-edge machine learning, recommendation systems, and product thinking, the team delivers highly relevant, personalized experiences to millions of listeners around the world.

    As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you will help shape the future of personalized discovery and engagement at Spotify.     We are currently looking for a new band member to join the Spotify Tax Team. This new band member will be an Analyst, joining the Global Indirect Tax Team. This position will report into the Senior Manager for Indirect Tax in EMEA and APAC and will be based in Stockholm, Sweden.

    In your role, you will focus on compliance and reporting. Spotify reports indirect taxes in more than 90 countries globally and you will be a key member of the team responsible for ensuring the completeness, timeliness and accuracy of Spotify’s global indirect tax compliance obligations. You will work in close collaboration with global tax team members in both Stockholm and New York, and work cross functionally with various accounting and finance teams.

    We are a team of highly skilled and dedicated colleagues and we offer a challenging and dynamic role in an ever changing environment with the opportunity to take on much responsibility in a rapidly growing international company. Above all, your work will impact the way the world experiences audio.

Tech.eu https://tech.eu en Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:23:24 +0000 hourly 1 <![CDATA[Startups respond to Britain's budget, Greentech Alliance acquires Intermobility, and Europe’s biggest seed rounds of Q3]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/startups-respond-to-britain-s-budget-greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-and-europe-s-biggest-seed-rounds-of-q3/ https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/startups-respond-to-britain-s-budget-greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-and-europe-s-biggest-seed-rounds-of-q3/#comments This week, we tracked more than 60 tech funding deals worth over €1.3 billion and over 10 exits, M&A transactions, rumours, and related news stories across Europe.

Britain has no shortage of startup ambition, but can it turn that success into companies that scale and stay? This week's UK Budget introduced Founders' Relief and a raft of measures supporting entrepreneurs, including expanded employee share options, initiatives for female founders and further investment in AI. It's a welcome signal, but tax incentives alone won't solve Britain's scaleup problem.

The UK attracted €14 billion in startup funding in H1 2026, yet access to later-stage capital, customers, talent and infrastructure remains a challenge.

In my follow-up feature, I spoke to founders and ecosystem leaders about what needs to change, from closing regional and gender funding gaps to helping companies commercialise and compete globally. The real test isn't how many startups Britain creates, but how many it can help grow into lasting global businesses.

Want to stay in the know? If email is more your thing, you can always subscribe to our newsletter and receive a more robust version of this round-up delivered to your inbox.

❗ Want to explore the data in more detail? The free, open-access Tech.eu Funding Explorer offers deeper insights into funding rounds, investor activity, company profiles and market trends.

Either way, let's get you up to speed.

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/startups-respond-to-britain-s-budget-greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-and-europe-s-biggest-seed-rounds-of-q3/ Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:23:24 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/startups-respond-to-britain-s-budget-greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-and-europe-s-biggest-seed-rounds-of-q3/feed 0 true <![CDATA[Beyond the lab: eight European healthtech scaleups taking on medicine’s biggest challenges]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/beyond-the-lab-eight-european-healthtech-scaleups-taking-on-medicines-biggest-challenges/ https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/beyond-the-lab-eight-european-healthtech-scaleups-taking-on-medicines-biggest-challenges/#comments European healthtech scaleups are tackling some of the industry’s most persistent challenges, from delayed diagnoses and overburdened hospitals to complex diseases with limited effective treatments.  

While their technologies and business models differ, they face a common challenge: translating scientific and engineering breakthroughs into clinically validated, commercially viable products that can reach patients across Europe and beyond, while navigating regulatory approval, healthcare system access and the substantial capital required to scale.

Here are some companies across a variety of verticals to have on your radar:

Diagnostics, AI and patient monitoring

Earlier diagnosis, more accurate assessments and continuous patient monitoring are critical against ageing populations, growing demand and shortages of medical professionals. However, their adoption requires demonstrable clinical value, clinical integration and the necessary regulatory approval and reimbursement.

Checkpoint Care (Bulgaria) 

Check Point Care develops remote patient monitoring tech. Its platform combines wearable medical devices, continuous physiological monitoring and AI-powered clinical decision support. It aims to reduce preventable deaths, hospital readmissions and pressure on healthcare systems by enabling earlier detection and intervention.

The company's wearable devices continuously collect clinical-grade data, including ECG, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate and body temperature.  This information is transmitted to a centralised digital platform, where AI algorithms analyse physiological patterns and generate digital biomarkers.

The system also creates personalised digital twins representing patients' physiological conditions, helping clinicians identify abnormalities and monitor changes over time.

A 24/7 Virtual Care Centre enables clinical teams to analyse patient data and communicate findings to treating physicians. 

Check Point Care’s tech has supported over 95,000 acute patients and analyses over 16.5 million data points monthly. 

Ligence (Lithuania)

Ligence develops AI-powered software that automates the analysis of cardiac ultrasound images, helping cardiologists assess heart function and identify potential abnormalities. Its flagship product, Ligence Heart, uses machine learning to analyse echocardiograms, automatically identify anatomical structures, perform measurements and generate structured reports. 

The company says its technology can reduce routine examination and reporting workflows from approximately 30 minutes to 15 minutes, potentially allowing hospitals to assess more patients without proportionally increasing staffing requirements.

The technology is designed to integrate with existing hospital imaging systems, reducing the manual work involved in cardiac diagnostics. Ligence has achieved European CE marking and two US FDA 510(k) clearances, the second granted in April 2026 for an updated version of Ligence Heart featuring automated left ventricular strain analysis. 

MiMARK Diagnostics (Spain)

MiMARK Diagnostics is developing molecular diagnostic technologies to improve the detection of gynaecological diseases, particularly endometrial cancer.  The company is focused on identifying disease-associated biomarkers in gynaecological samples to provide more accurate, less invasive diagnostic methods that can be incorporated into routine clinical practice.

Endometrial cancer is one of the most common gynaecological cancers, yet diagnosis can involve invasive procedures, including endometrial biopsies and hysteroscopy. More accessible testing could reduce unnecessary invasive procedures while supporting earlier identification of disease.

Medical devices and interventional technologies

Medical device innovation is transforming how clinicians treat serious conditions, particularly where conventional interventions are invasive, carry significant risks or have limited effectiveness. 

Anaconda Biomed ( Spain)

Barcelona-based Anaconda Biomed develops medical devices to treat acute ischaemic stroke, which occurs when a blood clot blocks an artery supplying the brain. Its technology focuses on mechanical thrombectomy, a minimally invasive procedure in which physicians use catheters to remove clots and restore blood flow.

The company's ANA Funnel Catheter features a self-expanding, funnel-shaped design intended to improve clot capture, restrict blood flow during retrieval and reduce the risk of clot fragments travelling into smaller vessels. Speed and effectiveness are critical in stroke treatment, as delays in restoring blood flow can result in permanent neurological damage, disability or death. 

Anaconda's tech works alongside existing thrombectomy devices, potentially improving the efficiency of clot removal and reducing complications. Its development reflects the growing importance of specialised neurovascular technologies that can improve outcomes in time-critical medical emergencies.

In September 2026, Anaconda Biomed secured $56 million in financing.

CorWave (France)

CorWave is developing implantable heart pumps for patients with advanced heart failure, using technology inspired by the movement of marine animals.  The technology is designed to reproduce more natural, pulsatile blood flow, adapting to the patient's 

Its Left Ventricular Assist System (LVAS) uses a patented wave membrane to propel blood through the device, rather than the rotary mechanisms used in conventional heart pumps. Existing ventricular assist devices can sustain patients for years, but risks such as bleeding, stroke and blood clot formation remain significant concerns.

CorWave aims to address these limitations by preserving the natural pulse and improving the interaction between mechanical circulatory support and the cardiovascular system. 

In May 2025 CoreWave’s LVAS was implanted in a patient for the first time at St Vincent's Hospital in Sydney, Australia. The patient successfully underwent a heart transplant after 84 days of mechanical support, with no device-related serious adverse events recorded at 30 days. 

Biotechnology and advanced therapeutics

Advances by European biotech companies in genomics, precision medicine, immunotherapy and cellular reprogramming are creating opportunities to target the underlying biological mechanisms of disease rather than simply managing symptoms. 

Arctic Therapeutics (Iceland)

Arctic Therapeutics is developing treatments for complex neurological and inflammatory diseases, drawing on genetic research and population-level health data to identify potential therapeutic targets. 

Its approach combines insights from human genetics with drug development to investigate disease mechanisms and identify opportunities for more targeted treatments.

By using genetic insights to understand the biological drivers of disease, Arctic Therapeutics aims to develop treatments that address underlying mechanisms rather than symptoms alone.

The company focuses on rare neurological diseases and forms of dementia. 

In 2025, Arctic Therapeutics raised €26.5 million Series A.

Asgard Therapeutics (Sweden)

Asgard Therapeutics is developing a new approach to cancer immunotherapy based on in vivo cellular reprogramming. 

Rather than relying solely on conventional treatments that directly attack tumours, the company is investigating how to reprogram cancer cells to stimulate the body's immune system, potentially enabling it to recognise and target malignant cells. Its technology aims to convert tumour cells into cells with antigen-presenting properties, allowing them to activate immune responses against cancer.

This approach could potentially address some of the limitations of existing immunotherapies, which do not work for every patient or cancer type.

Companies mentioned in this article are members of the EIC Scaling Club, a curated community where 120+ European deep tech scale-ups with the potential to build world-class businesses and solve major global challenges come together with investors, corporate innovators and other industry stakeholders to spur growth.

The EIC Scaling Club is an EIC-funded initiative run in partnership with Tech Tour, Bpifrance (EuroQuity), Hello Tomorrow, Tech.eu (Webrazzi), EurA and IESE Business School.

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/beyond-the-lab-eight-european-healthtech-scaleups-taking-on-medicines-biggest-challenges/ Fri, 30 Oct 2026 13:40:37 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/beyond-the-lab-eight-european-healthtech-scaleups-taking-on-medicines-biggest-challenges/feed 0 true <![CDATA[Greentech Alliance acquires Intermobility to tackle Europe's mobility coordination and funding gap]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-to-tackle-europe-s-mobility-coordination-and-funding-gap/ https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-to-tackle-europe-s-mobility-coordination-and-funding-gap/#comments Global connection network Greentech Alliance (GTA) has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Intermobility, a European transport and mobility network of more than 1,000 companies, public authorities and ecosystem players.  The deal creates a combined network of more than 5,000 members and partners in 25+ countries on six continents, linking climate investors, startups, corporates and policymakers in one of Europe's hardest sectors to decarbonise.

Founded in Berlin in May 2020 by Lubomila Jordanova, Simon Thies, Hannah Kromminga and Jan-Jaap Verhoeve, and led by CEO Charles Newton Price, the Alliance is a European and Canadian organisation, incorporated as both a Canadian not-for-profit and a German for-profit company, that operates globally. Its 3,000+ community members and partners represent more than 25 countries across six continents. GTA connects people, organisations, knowledge and capital through curated membership, trusted introductions, shared learning and programmes that extend beyond the network.

Transport is the laggard of Europe's climate transition. Its emissions were 25.3 per cent above 1990 levels in 2023 and made up around 31 per cent of the EU total, according to the European Environment Agency.  However, European mobility startups closed 654 funding rounds in 2025, down from 785 a year earlier, raising $10.1bn in total private funding.

The acquisition targets that gap. It puts Intermobility's operators, cities and public authorities in the same network as GTA's climate investors, startups and corporates, the groups that have to align before a mobility solution moves from pilot to scale.

For investors, GTA membership now offers curated access to mobility ventures from both communities and introductions to co-investors, corporates and public buyers.  For companies, it offers routes to customers, pilots and capital across Europe and internationally.

The two organisations will also explore joint ventures and financing projects, including work connected to Climate Zero programmes, subject to GTA's separate approval of each project.

According to Charles Newton Price, CEO, Greentech Alliance:

"Europe does not have a mobility technology problem, it has a coordination problem. The capital, the startups and the cities are all there, but they rarely meet.

Bringing Intermobility into Greentech Alliance puts the people who build, fund and buy mobility solutions in one network, and we are inviting investors and companies who want a seat at that table to join us."

Intermobility founder François Hoehlinger will join GTA's board, helping to shape the Alliance as it grows. 

He states:

"Mobility only changes when founders, investors, operators and public authorities move together. Intermobility built that table in Europe. Greentech Alliance gives it international reach and access to capital, while keeping a grounded European perspective at its heart." 

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-to-tackle-europe-s-mobility-coordination-and-funding-gap/ Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:51:59 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/greentech-alliance-acquires-intermobility-to-tackle-europe-s-mobility-coordination-and-funding-gap/feed 0 true <![CDATA[Iwoca CEO talks 15 years running a fintech, SME financing, and possible sale]]> https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/iwoca-ceo-talks-15-years-running-a-fintech-sme-financing-and-possible-sale/ https://tech.eu/2026/10/30/iwoca-ceo-talks-15-years-running-a-fintech-sme-financing-and-possible-sale/#comments “I will never forget it," says the long-standing CEO and co-founder of UK small business lender Iwoca, describing his meeting with one of the high priests of the European venture capital world. Christoph Rieche is a careful, measured speaker, so when he says “I will never forget it”, one tends to lock in.

Rewind to 2010ish, and Rieche, then a well-paid thirtysomething Goldman Sachs executive with itchy feet to launch a startup, met with Index Ventures co-founder Neil Rimer.

Rieche says: “Index was at the time already a pretty famous fund. I was in Geneva for business. Neil happened to be based there. I told him 'I can tell you about my world. Why don’t you tell me more about the VC world?' We were sitting in this meeting, and he said 'we just did an investment, but we haven’t announced it yet. It’s in a company called Funding Circle, and they provide lending to small businesses.’”

The revelation appears to have kick-started Rieche, who had been mulling launching his own Funding Circle AKA Iwoca, into action, as soon after Iwoca was born.

Turning the clock back

Tech.eu is sat opposite Rieche, who is German, in Iwoca’s newish, fresh-smelling London offices (all creams, soft furnishings, and overhanging plants), as the 46-year-old winds back the clock to Iwoca’s early days. Back then, he says, fintech wasn’t a thing; Revolut and Monzo weren’t about and the brands of the day were Spotify and LoveFilm while Rieche was a habitué of Meetup.com (now part of Bending Spoons) where he met his co-founder.

Rieche has now been CEO at Iwoca for nearly 15 years, which, he admits, is a long stint steering a startup or scaleup. But could it all be coming to an end?

Iwoca up for sale?

Sky News reported in June this year that Iwoca, which has raised around £70m in equity and is backed by Augmentum and Commerzbank’s CommerzVentures, was up for sale.

It had hired tech investment bank Qatalyst Partners to oversee the auction, with a sale value of over £1bn. 

Rieche says: “We have shareholders that have been with us for 15 years, some of them. Our last financing round was in 2019, so our youngest shareholder is seven years in. They are all VCs. These kinds of people naturally look for liquidity. It’s quite likely that we will find them some liquidity. But it doesn’t have any impact on our strategy.”

Does that mean an outright sale, IPO or secondary share sale? “I don’t know, these conversations happen literally all the time.”

Iwoca’s launch

You might not have heard of it, but Iwoca is one of the UK’s fastest-growing small business lenders, providing funding for tens of thousands of businesses every year.

It launched in 2012, when Rieche and his co-founder, James Dear, a former Deutsche Bank quant trader (who is stepping down this year), spied an opportunity in the ruins of the financial crisis, which saw banks retreat from SME lending.

Rieche says he was enticed by helping underserved SMEs, the overall market opportunity, and disrupting the legacy banks with tech and data. Today, Iwoca (whose name derives from its mission brief: instant working capital, so I-wo-ca), employs over 700 staff, with offices in London, Leeds, Berlin and Frankfurt.

Iwoca’s offering

Iwoca’s flagship product is SME loans, which range from £1,000 to £1,000,000 in the UK and up to €500,000 in Germany. Loan origination leapt from £952m to £1.5bn in 2025, driving up revenues by 56 per cent to £366m in 2025, Iwoca’s latest financial figures show.

Profits, meanwhile, nearly doubled from £59m to £113m in the period. Its jump in revenues comes amid incumbent banks retreating from SME financing, with challengers like Iwoca eating up market share.

Iwoca, which uses open banking to speed up loan applications, likes to trumpet the speed of its loan approval process, which is largely automated (its record is two minutes and three seconds from a standing start for an approval).

Starling deal

Iwoca also offers loans to Monzo, Starling and Tide customers and other businesses through partnership deals.

On its recently announced deal with Starling, Rieche said: “It’s been a long time in the making. I met Anne Boden about this more than 10 years go. I have been doing this for 15 years now. One thing I have learnt is that things take time. You can’t break through everything in a couple of days.”

One of the big trends in fintech in recent years has been the rise in stablecoin technology but Iwoca says it has no plans to leverage the tech in its lending offering.

Amid observers saying that Iwoca had too narrow an offering, it has recently expanded its product portfolio.

Flushed with “excess liquidity” and “more cognitive energy”, Iwoca has launched a credit score product, business credit card, and an M&A platform to help business buy and sell businesses.

Sanctioned shareholder

In Iwoca’s latest financial results, under the regulatory risk category, there is a reference to London-based VC Redline Capital, which is one of Iwoca’s longest-standing shareholder and owns around a 10 per cent stake in Iwoca. Redline was funded by Vladimir Yevtushenkov, a Russian oligarch, whose daughter Tatiana Evtushenkova has served as its CEO.

In 2023, Redline’s investment in Iwoca was placed under an asset freeze due to sanctions imposed by the UK government related to Yevtushenkov, the billionaire founder of Sistema, the Russian telecoms and media conglomerate

This caused “quite a big headache” for Iwoca, Rieche says. Evtushenkova, who stood down as director of Redline in 2023 according to filings, was removed from the UK sanctions list in 2025.

Rieche says: “These are the great experiences you go through when you are building your own company. Very fortunately for us, that person in the end was removed from the sanctions list last year, so we don’t have any sanctioned shareholders anymore. So, it’s a solved problem.”

Will Iwoca carry out future funding soon? Rieche says no, pointing to Iwoca being profitable.

Running a startup

German stereotypes aside, Rieche is initially a reserved interviewee and appears a methodical man (he did nine months “solid” startup and VC research and two work placements before launching Iwoca).

But once he gets going, he speaks fluidly about the ups and downs of his job (“there are times obviously when you are more motivated than others”), why he’s swerving conferences these days, and London losing its lustre as a fintech hub. Typically, Rieche works from 8.30am until around 8pm, with half his time on Iwoca’s UK business, the rest divided up between its German business and new initiatives.

Of late, he has pulled back on overseas work travel, as he has attending conferences.

He said: “There’s too much to do with the team. The ROI on these events, I think is reasonably low. I spend most of my time with the team and significantly less with the external world.”

Outside work, Rieche, who has two children, spends weekend driving his children around, as well as having an interest in London’s cultural scene.

London losing its appeal

On London as a fintech hub, he says, it has “probably got worse” since he started Iwoca, pointing to an increase in tax and pulling back of entrepreneurs’ incentives (the interview takes place the Autumn Budget).

He says: “Wherever I am looking, things got less flexible for businesses.”

That said, London will remain Iwoca’s headquarters and London “is still a phenomenal city and a magnet”.

The future 

Iwoca has hitherto served more than 100,000 SMEs with loans, but its big ambition is to serve one million.
